metadata.title: Secure High-Performance Computing

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for operating high-performance computing platforms that preserve isolation, attribution, data protection, and governed performance trade-offs across shared research and institutional workloads.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: High-performance computing clusters, batch schedulers, shared accelerators, interconnect fabrics, and associated data platforms.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Composite pattern asserting that all required platform, identity, job lifecycle, data protection, and governance trust requirements for HPC environments are satisfied.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Aggregate alignment with NIST SP 800-234 covering platform trust, identity, job lifecycle, data protection, performance trade-offs, and monitoring in HPC environments.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Privilege escalation risks arising from shared scheduler, compute node, or performance-optimized execution contexts.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Lateral movement across jobs, users, nodes, fabrics, or accelerators in shared HPC environments.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Unauthorized collection or inference of sensitive research data from shared HPC storage or residual execution state.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Abuse of valid accounts, including federated and non-interactive scheduler identities.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Privilege escalation via shared OS, scheduler, accelerator, or fabric execution contexts.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Execution isolation across shared compute nodes, jobs, and accelerators.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Separation of duties and explicit trust boundaries between users, schedulers, and administrators.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Lifecycle management to reduce residual data and execution-state exposure after job completion.

metadata.remarks: Secure High-Performance Computing is a composite trust pattern asserting that shared execution risk, scheduler-mediated authority, job lifecycle security, data protection, accelerator and fabric trust, behavioral monitoring, and explicit performance risk governance are collectively satisfied for HPC platforms. This pattern introduces no independent controls and exists solely as an aggregate trust claim for SSPPs, solution architectures, and institutional risk governance.

components.title: HPC Federated Access Trust
components.remarks: Applicable only where external or cross-institution access is supported.
